title: Deep Harmonic Finesse: Signal Separation in Wearable Systems with Limited Data
problem: Separate overlapping quasi-periodic physiological signals in wearable systems when limited training data is available. In applications like fetal monitoring, multiple vital signs mix into sensed signals, making isolation difficult without extensive data collection.
motivation: Wearable health monitoring systems require accurate signal separation with minimal data collection due to practical constraints and power limitations in real-world deployments.
method: Uses a deep harmonic neural network with embedded harmonic priors in the time-frequency domain to mask and in-paint spectrograms. A pattern-alignment component transforms sensed signals to align with the network structure. The approach leverages prior knowledge of expected time-frequency patterns in physiological signals to enable effective separation with limited training data.
key_novelty: Embedding implicit harmonic priors within a deep neural network's time-frequency architecture to enable signal separation with minimal training data in wearable systems.
contributions: Deep harmonic neural network architecture with embedded harmonic priors for time-frequency analysis
Pattern alignment method for transforming sensed signals to network specifications
Spectrogram masking and in-painting approach for limited-data signal separation
Demonstration on non-invasive fetal monitoring with 26-80% improvements on synthetic data and 80.5% improvement on in vivo blood oxygen saturation estimation

metrics.accuracy: 26% SDR improvement, 80% MSE improvement (synthetic), 80.5% correlation error improvement (in vivo)

limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed; approach requires prior knowledge of signal time-frequency patterns and is primarily validated on fetal monitoring applications.
primary_theme: Deep learning for limited-data physiological signal separation in wearables
